title: Fan-out pattern: spreading work across goroutines

videos.script: This lesson starts the patterns. The first is fan-out: several goroutines reading the same channel. {{spread}} You send twelve jobs to three workers. Nobody deals them out. Whichever worker is free takes the next job. Every job is done exactly once, and the split changes from run to run, because it follows speed. {{order}} Then the price. Results come back in the order the work finished, not the order it started. Two short words beat two long ones. You get the order back in two ways: an index on each result, or a slice where each goroutine writes only its own place. {{errors}} Last, failure. Twenty files, four workers, two damaged files. The first error cancels the rest. The context keeps the reason. And errors.Join keeps the ones that were already on their way. {{close}} Lesson 14 does the opposite: many channels merged into one.
